claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed potential would be developed using data or simulations from DFT or molecular dynamics.
The approach applies to high-temperature solid and liquid phases.
Atomic structure and chemical composition act as the structural mediator connecting the model to predicted thermodynamic behavior.
The machine-learning potential can capture complex interatomic interactions in high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning potential can capture correlations among atoms in high-entropy alloys.
Capturing complex atomic interactions and correlations enables accurate prediction of thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach will determine high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties more efficiently than existing experimental and theoretical methods.
The proposed approach will determine high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties more accurately than existing experimental and theoretical methods.
The proposed approach is expected to reduce prediction error by 10–20% relative to existing methods.
Applicability is limited to high-entropy alloys with known chemical composition and atomic structure.
Accuracy is particularly uncertain for high-entropy alloys having complex or unknown composition or atomic structure.
The approach can be tested by comparing predictions against experimental measurements for a set of high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is deemed falsified if predicted thermodynamic properties deviate from experimental measurements by more than 20%.
